shouldFix.title: The frozen review identity is not bound to the subject bytes it reviewed
evidence: Every round register from v8 onward carries subjectSha256, recordedInputs carries the canonical subject path/hash, and all 34 frozen lane files from v6 through v22 carry subjectSha256AtStart and subjectSha256AtEnd. roundLaneIdentity nevertheless checks only that subject or reviewOf, if present, names host-effect-authorization.vN. Neither it nor provenanceCheck compares any review-declared subject digest with predecessorVerdictFindings[N].subjectSha256 or recordedInputs[the vN subject path].

A concrete in-memory countermodel starts from the canonical frozen v22 Codex review and changes subjectSha256Expected, subjectSha256AtStart, and subjectSha256AtEnd from the v22 digest ff4d4f24... to the v21 digest 25e18ce6..., leaving subject=docs/coop/artifacts/host-effect-authorization.v22.json, reviewer=Codex, reviewStatus=COMPLETE, verdict=REJECT, and all findings unchanged. The resulting review bytes hash to 6ac7b100818206b782e821b97eb86e41589d856ab993a56f389567eee5bd50a1; recording that hash in the lane and recordedInputs satisfies the review-file provenance check even though the review expressly attests to different subject bytes.

That countermodel still passes canonical path, round-name, reviewer-lane, terminal status, verdict eligibility, finding extraction, pair equality, dispositions, and FromVN coverage. predecessorVerdictFindings.v22.subjectSha256 can remain the real v22 hash because no governing check connects it to the review's start/end/expected hashes.

The omission is not required for legacy compatibility. Every actual review from v6 through v22 has both subjectSha256AtStart and subjectSha256AtEnd, and each pair is equal. Requiring those members would cover the entire governed corpus without an exception.

The live v22 data is sound: both frozen reviews reproduce at their dispatched hashes, name the canonical v22 subject, and have expected/start/end subject digests equal to the registered and recorded v22 digest. That bounds the defect to SHOULD-FIX rather than a blocker.
shouldFix.impact: A correctly named, canonical-path, COMPLETE frozen review can be registered as evidence for subject N even when it reviewed different bytes. Later lineage can therefore preserve every review-file and finding pin while attributing a verdict to a subject revision the reviewer never examined, defeating the byte-custody guarantee behind independent review.
shouldFix.requiredRepair: Add a subjectDigestIdentity check before extraction. Require predecessorVerdictFindings[N].subjectSha256 to equal recordedInputs[docs/coop/artifacts/host-effect-authorization.vN.json]. Require every pinned review's subjectSha256AtStart and subjectSha256AtEnd to be present canonical sha256 strings and equal that same digest; if subjectSha256Expected is present, require it to equal as well. Any absent, malformed, start/end mismatch, or mismatch with the registered subject pin MUST refuse. Keep the existing subject-name and reviewer-lane checks.
